name: Red Beans and Rice
equipment: Large stockpot, separate pan for rice
notes: Dad (Mark) said this was pretty authentic compared to the normal fare he experienced as a missionary in Louisiana. Note: if you don’t have any Cajun seasoning, you can make your own using a basic recipe from online. It’s just a blend of a few other spices.

items: 1 package (13ish oz) smoked sausage, thinly sliced
3 (15 oz) cans red beans, drained and rinsed

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.body: Get the water and rice started in a separate pan: **1 cup basmati rice**.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.body: Heat **1 Tbsp vegetable oil** in a large stockpot and add **1 package (13ish oz) smoked sausage, thinly sliced**, stirring frequently until sausage is lightly browned. Set sausage aside.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.body: Add **1 medium sweet onion, diced**, **1 green bell pepper, diced** and **2 celery ribs, diced** to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.body: Add **2 Tbsp tomato paste**, **3 cloves garlic, minced** and **1½ tsp Cajun seasoning** for an additional 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.body: Stir in **3 (15 oz) cans red beans, drained and rinsed**, **3 cups chicken stock**, **1 tsp hot sauce**, **1 bay leaf** and the cooked sausage; season with salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil; cover, reduce heat, and simmer for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.body: Uncover, continue to simmer until reduced, an additional 15 minutes.

steps.title: Mash and serve
steps.body: Using a wooden spoon, mash beans until slightly thickened. Serve immediately, topped with rice.
